titulo: A machine that pulls drinking water out of the air.
titulo_aba: HydraSource Review — Water From Air, Tested
subtitulo: It sounds like a gimmick. I ran one for a week to find out how much water it really makes — and where it disappoints.
meta_descricao: An atmospheric water generator tested for a week: how much water it really makes, and where it falls short.

texto:
The physics here isn't magic: the unit chills a surface until moisture in the air condenses on it, then filters what it collects. Dehumidifiers have done the first half for decades. What you're paying for is the filtration and the convenience of having it come out drinkable.

In a normally humid room, mine produced a bit under two gallons a day — enough for a household's drinking water, not enough to cook and clean with. It also runs constantly, and you will hear it. It's about as loud as a window air conditioner.

Where it genuinely earned its place: no more hauling cases of bottled water, and no plastic piling up by the door. Whether that's worth the price depends entirely on where you live — which is what the next section is about.

como_funciona.titulo: Plug it into a standard outlet
como_funciona.texto: No plumbing, no installation. It needs a power socket and room to breathe.

como_funciona.titulo: It condenses moisture from the air
como_funciona.texto: A cooled coil pulls humidity out of the room, the same principle as a dehumidifier.

como_funciona.titulo: The water is filtered into the tank
como_funciona.texto: Multi-stage filtration before it reaches the dispenser. Filters are replaceable.

nao_e_para_voce: You live somewhere dry — below about 40% humidity, output drops sharply
You need water for cooking and cleaning, not just drinking
Electricity costs are a major concern — it runs continuously
You need it silent. It isn't.
nao_e_para_voce_nota: If none of those are dealbreakers for you, it's a genuinely useful machine.

faq.resposta: You'll be taken to the official HydraSource website, where the order is processed. I don't handle payment, shipping or returns — the manufacturer does.

faq.pergunta: How much water does it actually make?
faq.resposta: In my testing, a little under two gallons per day in a normally humid room. Output depends heavily on temperature and humidity, so treat any single number as a ceiling rather than a promise.

faq.pergunta: Does it work in a dry climate?
faq.resposta: Less well. Below roughly 40% relative humidity, production falls off noticeably. If you live somewhere arid, this is the wrong product for you.

faq.pergunta: How often do filters need replacing?
faq.resposta: Roughly every six months under normal use. Factor the replacement cost into your decision — it's an ongoing expense, not a one-time purchase.
